name: Motorcycle
description: A motor vehicle with a seat or saddle designed to travel on no more than three wheels; an electric one whose motor produces more than 5 brake horsepower (about 3,730 W) is a full motorcycle rather than a motor-driven cycle. Defined by Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes Title 75 §102.
restrictions: A seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground
Its motor produces more than 5 brake horsepower (about 3,730 W)
Riders need a Class M license
Riders under 21 must wear a motorcycle helmet, as must older riders unless they've held a motorcycle license for two years or completed an approved rider safety course
Titled and registered with PennDOT for $18 a year, with the registration card carried while riding, and must carry insurance

Pennsylvania has no off-highway motorcycle category: its ATV law excludes trail bikes, and an off-road electric dirt bike without a VIN can't be registered, so it's ridden only on private property or trails that allow it
